archetype.name: Dual-Threat (developing passer)
archetype.definition: A second-year quarterback whose legs were a top-tier weapon as a rookie, and who opened 2026 showing a quicker, more accurate short-to-intermediate passing game than he had last year.

report.headline: One brilliant game against the league's worst defense, then IR and QB3
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 line ranks first in the league in EPA per dropback (0.522), completion rate and TD rate, and none of it should be read at face value. Nearly all of it comes from Week 1 against Dallas, a defense that now ranks 32nd. He went 23 of 29 for three scores and +19.7 passing EPA in that game. In Week 2 at the Rams he played 12% of the snaps, threw five passes, and has not appeared since. He did not practice in Week 3, the site lists him on injured reserve, and the depth chart as of November 17 has him third. Jameis Winston started four games and J.J. McCarthy has started since Week 7. The question now is whether he gets his job back, not how good his season is.

The opener still showed real progress worth noting. As a rookie he was a run-first creator with a shaky arm: third in the league in rushing yards (487) but 35th in CPOE, with a 15% bad-throw rate. Against Dallas he got the ball out faster (2.64 seconds against 2.82 last year), threw a little more aggressively, and was precise in the 10-19 yard window: 1.035 EPA on 11 throws, 72.7% completions, 19 points over expected. He went 9 of 9 for conversions-plus on third down and 7 for 7 in the red zone with three scores. Isaiah Likely was the main beneficiary at 1.201 EPA per target. The designed runs held up too: 8.17 yards a carry, every one a success.

What the numbers hide is how small and soft the sample is. It is 34 attempts, and almost all of them came against the worst defense in the league. His deep passing was 0 for 3. The habit that cost him as a rookie also showed up: a pressure-to-sack rate of 33.3% ranks 28th of 42, close to last year's 36.5%, which ranked 43rd of 62. That is partly the cost of a scrambler holding the ball to make something happen. But his two scrambles this year produced 10 yards and no first downs, so the trade did not pay.

The outlook depends on health and the depth chart. If he gets back on the field and back into the lineup, expect something close to his rookie baseline, with somewhat better accuracy, rather than the Week 1 numbers. A Giants offense that is 26th in pass rate over expected under John Harbaugh will lean on his legs and the short game, not on volume passing.

strengths.title: Designed runs that move the chains
strengths.body: His rookie season put him third in the league in rushing yards. This year's six designed runs produced big chunks with no stuffs. The rushing is the steadiest part of his profile across both seasons, so it should hold up whenever he plays, as long as he is healthy enough to run.

strengths.title: Sharper short-to-intermediate accuracy
strengths.body: He threw faster and more accurately than as a rookie, and he was especially efficient over the middle and in the 10-19 yard window. Part of the gain is probably real growth in year two, given the quicker clock and the lower bad-throw rate. Part of it is Dallas's defense. Expect his CPOE to settle somewhere above last year's rather than staying near the top of the league.

strengths.title: Early chemistry with Isaiah Likely
strengths.body: Likely tied Malik Nabers for the team lead with nine targets and produced more than twice Nabers's EPA per target. Dart found the tight end on intermediate in-breakers and on third downs. That is a usable read, but it comes from one game.

concerns.title: No longer the starter
concerns.body: He is on injured reserve and listed third on the depth chart, behind two quarterbacks who have taken every start since Week 3, with McCarthy the current starter. Even after he is healthy, getting the job back is not a given. This matters more than anything in his stat line.

concerns.title: A season built on one soft opponent
concerns.body: Almost all of his production came against the defense now ranked 32nd. His only other appearance was a 20-yard cameo against the Rams, who rank 3rd. The league-leading efficiency ranks are a one-game snapshot and should not be projected forward.

concerns.title: Pressure still turns into sacks
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate stayed in the bottom half of the league for the second straight year, so this is a lasting trait rather than noise. It is the cost of a creator extending plays, but this year the scrambles did not pay for it, and he was 0 for 3 throwing deep. Behind a line that ranks 29th in hit rate allowed, the problem won't fix itself.

trend.note: His season peaked with a 26.6-point opener against Dallas. He played 12% of the snaps in Week 2, missed Week 3 practice, and has been on IR and out of the rotation since, with two other quarterbacks starting.

nextGame.headline: Unlikely to play; Jacksonville's defense is built against his game
nextGame.body:
Dart is on IR and third on the depth chart, so a Week 11 appearance against Jacksonville is unlikely. If he did play, the matchup works against what he does well. Jacksonville allows the lowest EPA in the league on short passes, is the stingiest defense against a team's top tight end, and ranks 3rd against the run. That shuts down the quick game, the Likely connection and his designed runs. Its one weakness is deep passing, where it ranks 28th, and that is the area where Dart went 0 for 3. The Book has the Giants as 6-point home underdogs at +215.

The Giants' own injury report is empty, so this comes down to Dart's status and the coaches' choice at quarterback. On Jacksonville's side, center Robert Hainsey (knee) is listed questionable, which affects their offense rather than Dart's matchup. The two questionable or IR defensive ends are rotation players with little or no snap share, so the pass rush he would face is largely intact.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs. the league's best
keyMatchups.body: Most of Dart's value came on throws under 10 air yards, and Jacksonville is the hardest defense in the league to beat there. A quarterback with his profile would have to push the ball downfield against them, which he has not done well.

keyMatchups.title: Likely against a stingy TE defense
keyMatchups.body: His most productive target this year was the tight end, and Jacksonville ranks first against top tight ends by EPA per play. Even a healthy Dart would lose his best read.

keyMatchups.title: Run defense limits his legs
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville's 3rd-ranked run defense meets a Giants rushing attack that ranks 20th. That makes it hard for any Giants quarterback to rely on designed runs.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart is activated from IR and moves up the depth chart, or McCarthy stays the starter.

restOfSeason.body:
The rest of his season depends on availability, not efficiency. He is on IR and third on the depth chart, so the most likely outcome is little or no playing time until something changes at the top. If he does return and win the job back, plan on his rookie baseline with modest accuracy gains, not the Week 1 line. Expect roughly 165-210 passing yards a game, about one TD, and a meaningful rushing contribution of 30-45 yards a game.

The TD rate, the 76.5% completion rate and the zero interceptions all rest on 34 attempts and will regress. The rushing value and the faster release have the better chance to last. The pressure-to-sack habit has held for two seasons and will keep costing drives behind a line that allows hits.
swingFactors: Return from IR and his health
Whether coaches go back to him over McCarthy
Whether the improved accuracy holds against real defenses

confidence.note: One full game and a cameo, IR, and third on the depth chart.
